records.historicalPeriodLabel: Bronze Age Crete; palatial phases chiefly in the second millennium BCE

phases.text: Palatial centres emerged around 1900 BCE. This is an archaeological development, not a documented coronation or island-wide unification.
The Neopalatial phase is conventionally dated approximately 1700-1450 BCE; centres had distinct local histories.
Zominthos developed around 1700 BCE; the surviving Malia complex around 1650 BCE; Zakros around 1500 BCE. These are site dates.
Destructions around 1450 BCE were followed by stronger Mycenaean influence and Greek-language Linear B administration. Causes and political mechanisms remain debated.
Kydonia remained significant in the Mycenaean era. A single destruction date cannot stand for all Cretan communities.

uncertainty: Palatial centres are not proven provinces of one kingdom.
Do not use imported -4000 or -1500 as a civilization foundation or extinction date.
The UNESCO site ensemble date range is not an exact political lifetime.

records.historicalPeriodLabel: First millennium BCE, with varied local transitions under Roman rule

phases.text: Villanovan archaeological traditions preceded and overlapped the development of identifiable Etruscan language and urban society.
Etruria contained independent cities including Veii, Cerveteri, Tarquinia and Vulci, with different local trajectories.
Veii was conquered by Rome in 396 BCE. This proposed date concerns one city.
Volsinii was attacked by Rome in 264 BCE; this represents a later local transition, not the fall of every Etruscan community.
Roman expansion brought a prolonged process of political incorporation and cultural interaction.

endingOrContinuity.successorIdentityProposal: Roman Republic, with separate local transitions

uncertainty: Do not assign one conquest date to all Etruscan cities.
Cultural continuity must be researched separately from autonomy.
Imported -500 to -323 misses earlier and later evidence.

records.historicalPeriodLabel: Poleis developed during the early first millennium BCE and continued in later political settings

phases.text: Polis institutions developed during the Geometric period, approximately 900-700 BCE.
Shared sanctuaries and cultural practices linked communities with distinct civic identities.
Alexander's death in 323 BCE conventionally starts the Hellenistic period; it did not terminate every polis.
Some cities pursued autonomy through the Aetolian and Achaean leagues amid successor kingdoms.

uncertainty: Separate Athens, Sparta, Corinth and leagues before political successor links.
Imported -1500 includes an inappropriate blanket polis label for Bronze Age societies.
No collective fall in 200 BCE established.

records.historicalPeriodLabel: Merovingian and early Carolingian kingdoms, with earlier Frankish antecedents

phases.text: Clovis's sons divided his realm after his death in 511.
Reunifications under Chlothar I and Chlothar II alternated with partitions; Austrasia, Neustria and Burgundy require separate phases.
Childeric III was removed and Pepin became king; 751 is the proposed modern date for this dynastic change.
Charlemagne became king in 768 and received the imperial title in 800.

uncertainty: A change of dynasty is not extinction of Frankish society.
The franks and frankish-kingdom imports need identity reconciliation.
Earlier exact regnal dates await specialist confirmation.

records.historicalPeriodLabel: Imperial title from 800; partitions and successor kingdoms during the ninth century

phases.text: Charlemagne received the imperial title in 800, after decades as a Frankish king.
The settlement at Verdun in 843 divided rule among Lothar, Louis and Charles.
Middle Francia was further partitioned in 855.
Charles the Fat's deposition in 887 is a proposed endpoint for the last broad reunification, not for every Carolingian dynasty or institution.

uncertainty: Existing successor polygons begin at 900, not at the proposed 843 transition.
Distinguish imperial title, political union and dynasty.
Later ninth-century chronology needs better corroboration before release.

records.historicalPeriodLabel: Late fifth to mid-sixth century; exact endpoints pending independent chronology review

phases.text: Theodoric's defeat of Odoacer in 493 is the proposed start of his established Italian kingdom.
After Theodoric died in 526, Athalaric succeeded under Amalasuntha's regency.
Eastern Roman intervention began in 535; the capture of Ravenna in 540 did not end all Gothic resistance or kingship.
Major royal defeats occurred in 552-553. A precise final year requires reconciliation of battle dates and surviving resistance.
Ravenna preserves distinct Ostrogothic and Byzantine building phases.

endingOrContinuity.crossRegionalReview: QWEN or Asia owner must review successor identity before activation

uncertainty: The imported 500-700 interval does not establish the kingdom lifetime.
Ethnic identity did not disappear on a single battlefield date.
General encyclopedia contradictions prohibit automatic exact fall metadata.

records.historicalPeriodLabel: Documented before 800; autonomy and regional administration changed during the ninth and tenth centuries

phases.text: Penda and Offa belong to Mercian history before the imported map record begins. Exact early dates need specialist confirmation.
Offa's Dyke was probably constructed in the 780s, demonstrating substantial activity before 800.
The Chronicle records Burgred's removal and Ceolwulf's installation in its annal for 874.
The Chronicle places a division of Mercia between the army and Ceolwulf in 877.
Aethelflaed and then her daughter held Mercian authority before Edward assumed direct control; chronicle variants require reconciliation around 918-920.

endingOrContinuity.successorIdentityProposal: Scandinavian-controlled eastern districts and the expanding English kingdom at different dates

uncertainty: No securely demonstrated exact foundation date adopted.
Do not flatten partition, loss of royal independence and later regional identity into one fall.
825 and 918 remain proposed dates requiring independent modern confirmation.

records.historicalPeriodLabel: Seventh-century kingdom and later northern English regimes; regional transitions differ

phases.text: Northumbria joined Deira and Bernicia; the precise timing and reversals of union need separate phases.
Oswald ruled from 634 and supported Aidan's foundation at Lindisfarne in 635.
The Synod of Whitby in 664 belongs to a well-established Northumbrian political and religious setting.
The Chronicle records the defeat and deaths of rival Northumbrian kings at York in 867.
Its annal for 954 records Eric's expulsion and Edred's assumption of Northumbrian government.

uncertainty: Bernicia/Bamburgh and York require separate post-867 treatment.
Monastery evacuation is not a kingdom fall.
Existing England map record starts at 1000, not 954; proposed link cannot imply a verified polygon for 954.

records.historicalPeriodLabel: Early medieval West Saxon kingdom; later transformation into wider English kingship

phases.text: Alfred's law collection drew on earlier royal laws, including those of Ine, demonstrating a history before the 800 map snapshot.
Alfred became king in 871.
The Chronicle describes a severe crisis and Alfred's recovery in 878; this was not a permanent termination of Wessex.
Alfred took control of London in 886, within a developing wider English political identity.
Athelstan's takeover of York in 927-928 belongs to the expansion of English kingship, not the conquest of Wessex by an unrelated successor civilization.

uncertainty: No legendary exact foundation date adopted.
A tenth-century successor needs an identity phase before the imported England polygon begins in 1000.
West Saxon regional identity and ruling dynasty did not simply disappear.
